assets.content:
Subject: Does trial signup tracking need code?
Preview text: Only when the signup flow has no distinct confirmation page. Here is how to choose the right goal.

Hi there,

Turn trial signup completion into a goal and see where those signups came from. Plausible Analytics is a privacy-friendly web analytics tool that shows website traffic and signup conversions in one dashboard.

If signup ends on a distinct confirmation page, set that page as a pageview goal with no code changes. If there is no distinct page, use a custom event goal, which requires a code snippet or script.

After the first conversion is recorded, the goal appears in the Goals section. Filter the dashboard by that goal to review conversion rate, referrer sources, entry pages and the pages where visitors converted.

Inspect the official goal-conversions guide to decide whether your signup should use a pageview goal or a custom event goal.

Inspect the goal-conversions guide →

- the Plausible Analytics team

brief.interpretation: A single introductory evaluation email for a solution-aware small SaaS owner, focused on tracking trial-signup conversions rather than selling a broader analytics migration or promising conversion improvement.
brief.reader:
Selected audience: Small SaaS website owner measuring signup conversion.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (grounded; check applicability): Small SaaS website owners who already have a live product with public pricing and signup pages, and who track and publicly report their own visitor-to-signup and trial-to-paid conversion numbers, often after a launch spike or after changing their signup flow.
brief.reader_segment: Small SaaS website owner measuring signup conversion
brief.promise: Plausible can turn trial signup completion into a conversion goal and show which sources and entry pages contributed to those signups.
brief.orientation: Plausible Analytics is a privacy-friendly web analytics tool for viewing website traffic and signup conversions in one dashboard.
brief.arc: Introduce Plausible through one useful task, explain the smallest appropriate setup choice, show what becomes visible after a conversion, and send the reader to the official setup guide.
brief.sequence_rationale: One email is sufficient because the requested outcome is a focused first evaluation, not a nurture sequence. The argument begins with the reader's signup question, gives a conditional first step that does not assume their site implementation, and ends with a read-only documentation CTA. No objection is assigned beyond setup uncertainty because the evidence does not establish this recipient's current analytics tool, workflow, or migration concerns.

emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the official guide and determine whether their signup should be tracked with a pageview goal or a custom event goal.
emails.single_idea: Define trial signup completion as a Plausible goal, then use the goal-filtered dashboard to see which referrer sources and entry pages produced those conversions.
emails.felt_need: Free-trial signups do not convert to paid at a rate the owner considers acceptable, even after a signup surge.
emails.status_quo: They add free trials that require a payment method upfront to try to convert website visitors into paying customers.
emails.mechanism: If signup completion reaches a distinct confirmation page, the reader can set that page as a pageview goal without changing code; if it does not, the guide explains the custom-event route. After the first recorded conversion, the goal appears in the Goals section and can filter the dashboard to reveal conversion rate, referrer sources, entry pages and top converting pages.
emails.belief_shift: Before: understanding signup acquisition may feel like a broad analytics project. After: the reader sees one bounded first decision—choose the appropriate goal type—and knows what source and landing-page information it can unlock.
must_not_say: Do not presume which analytics tool, if any, the reader currently uses.
Do not presume the reader's traffic volume, conversion rate, privacy compliance status or technical stack.
Do not claim that Plausible will increase signups, improve conversion rates or reproduce Plausible's own measured results.
Do not use Plausible's 84% signup increase as proof that goal tracking caused a lift.
Do not imply that every signup flow can use a no-code pageview goal; custom event goals require a code snippet or script.
Do not expand into pricing, migration, funnels, trial-to-paid benchmarks, privacy compliance, uptime or the broader feature set.
emails.objection: The reader may be unsure whether their signup flow needs code to track.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the signup should be configured as a pageview goal or a custom event goal.
emails.next_step_value: The guide explains the two goal types and how to set up and measure a conversion goal.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the guide does not configure the reader's site, record a conversion or establish that tracking will improve signup performance.
emails.subject_strategy: Name the concrete outcome—seeing where trial signups come from—without implying a benchmark, existing analytics problem or guaranteed lift.

brief.voice_notes: Use short, direct paragraphs and the product terms “goal,” “pageview goal,” “custom event goal” and “dashboard.” Avoid hype and the phrase “Get started.”
